item.content:encoded:
Timer Removed. Edits Made. See Discussion Below.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 72 hours if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. + Show Block
- Hide Block

There is a lot of potential for crosslinks in a robo-arm that allows you to literally grab someone's soul, and stick it into something else. The article itself already has an addendum in which it is suggested that the object could be used to replicate other objects (especially ones that are basically thing what has a human soul inside it.) That being said, I propose expanding this brief section to include additional examples:

Recommending changing the following:

Addendum-01: Dr. ██████████ suggests experimentation with D-class personnel and electronic equipment, to attempt to reproduce SCP-168 or similar phenomena. (Pending)

To:

Addendum-01: Dr. ██████████ suggests experimentation with D-class personnel and electronic equipment, to attempt to reproduce SCP-168, SCP-696, SCP-1875, or similar phenomena. (Pending)

Obviously there are other articles that come to mind that could work for this kind of crosslink, such as SCP-2306, but lets not get too bogged down with links and leave it at a total of three.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: Re: Idea
item.content:encoded:
Note: All this is my headcanon, please don't be offended if you don't agree.
I think their logic for most SCPs is "if we don't need to kill it, don't kill it because what if another one appears and we can't deal with it." SCPs like 682 and 096 are exceptions because they've been confirmed to be a severe, hard-to-contain threat and have little research and scientific value. I suppose we could use 158 on 096 but the problem is you'd have to do the entire procedure without looking at 096's face. I personally don't like the idea of using it on Cassy because in my mind the subject's happiness is not the Foundation's primary concern, but rather it comes after humanity's safety and research.

item.title: Re: Idea
item.content:encoded:
Well, there's something making it move, whatever it is. It could be worth a shot… so long that shot is done far away from anywhere populated, to avoid another explosion.
I also thought on using it on 49, 96 and other dangerous SCPs. Oh, and what about 126? She's invisible and tangible, but she have some sort of soul, being a ghost and all.

Well, they have tried killing 682 and have scheduled 96 for termination, so saying SCP doesn't try killing or normalizing stuff is erroneous.
Besides, SCP has been taking care of Cassy for a while now, and she is completely harmless. We could give her a human body and have her work as a mechanic for us.
Food for thought, anyway.

item.title: Re: Idea
item.content:encoded: I'm not sure 173 even has a soul in the conventional sense of the word, it's animate but not really alive. Also it might actually work on Cassy, but the Foundation's goal is to contain anomalies, not destroy/normalize them. While it might be a nice thing to do, it's not how the Foundation works.

item.title: Idea
item.content:encoded:
I was about to suggest using this thing on 682, but I read the other comments, so forget that!

But then I thought… what about 173? Could it remove his soul, leave it a unmoving statue? Or is there risk of a repeat of 682 incident?

Also, I was reading on 85/Cassy before I got to 158 and I thought on how we could try extracting her soul from the drawing, if that could be done, and reverse it on a vacant human body? I worry about the risks, and I wouldn't want to hurt Cassy, so if no one wants to risk it, that's fine too. So far, aside from 682, there weren't been any failed extractions or reversals, or they weren't included in the file. Were there any case of failed soul switches or side-effects?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
5) Souls wouldn't work on the device. Because of either it's abilities, the nature or items of its construction, it's immune to possession.

6) A pile of sand wouldn't because it's not a solid object. The criteria for possession is that the host object must be a mainly solid body, although some liquids can be possessed so long as they're in a container. The host object has to be big enough to accommodate the soul, and the object also must be something affected by human hands. It can't be something random like an odd rock.

7) It either gets jammed in the machine and dissipates, or gets stuck in there until it can be extracted.

8) It could probably modify, combine, alter souls, but since most of the manual was destroyed no one really knows how to do it, and they're a little wary of destroying the device through misuse.

9) It'd go through all the actions, but the there'd be no soul at the end of it. Like trying to wring blood from a stone.

Again, thanks!

Some more questions:

5) What is the effect of extracted souls on the machine itself? i.e. can the machine itself be "possessed"?

7) What happens to the soul of the subject if the machine is operated unsuccessfully?

8) Does the machine do more than extract and replace souls?

9) Does the machine "choke" if used on something lacking a soul? Such as a rock?

That's all for now.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Wow, thanks man.

1) As for the extra souls in a single body, you'd most likely get a type of extreme multiple personality disorder, with the souls vying for dominance of the body. The stronger, or more enthusiastic ones would be at the forefront most of the time, and the weaker, apathetic ones would be dormant more often.

2) The item would become sentient, but behave like a ghost, in the sense that it would "haunt" the surrounding area.

3) For artificial intelligence…. Well, that's a whole can of worms there. It depends on the question, can a machine created by man possess a soul? Not an SCP machine mind you, just a machine. So I'm not exactly sure about that one myself. Possibly if the program was one that was engineered to learn, to have emotions and feelings and memories and such.

4) Well, I'd guess you'd have either a single person in charge of two bodies, a pair of people who cannot mentally carry on without the other, or some mixture of the two.

Like I said, thanks!
